A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Voxify3D and contain readable main text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices A–E. Relocated and renumbered material can be matched reliably across the complete 19-page versions.

before.justification: v1 reports original mesh-stylization experiments, CLIP-IQA measurements, component ablations, and user studies with 72 participants and 10 art-trained participants.

after.justification: v2 retains these empirical results and additionally reports quantitative component ablations averaged over five objects in Table 2.

M1.justification: Section 3 and Appendix B retain the two-stage DVGO pipeline, orthographic supervision, loss functions, and Gumbel-Softmax color assignment. RGB-based logit initialization and rare-color boosting were already documented in v1’s appendix.

E1.justification: Both versions retain Rodin, Unique3D, and TRELLIS, with the same mesh-to-voxel task, object domains, and palette/resolution scenarios. The added component scores do not establish additional dataset or task coverage.

E2.justification: The four main baselines and the appendix comparisons with Gemini 3 and Rodin remain. Appendix C removes the numerical runtime comparison against SD-piXL, previously approximately four hours, replacing it with an unquantified comparison to manual creation.

E3.justification: v2 adds a five-object quantitative evaluation of the full model and six ablated configurations in Table 2. The existing 35-case benchmark, user-study samples, and training budgets remain unchanged. The newly stated 1200 × 1200 rendering resolution is additional documentation rather than evidence of a changed setting.

E4.justification: v1 provides qualitative component removals and quantitative resolution-dependent CLIP-loss ablations. v2 substantially strengthens component analysis by quantifying all six stage/component removals in Table 2 and comparing them on two shared inputs in Figure 6. The original resolution analysis remains as appendix Table 7.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The new five-object averages continue the existing point-estimate reporting practice without adding uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: New Table 2 reports 40.06 for the full model and ablation scores ranging from 27.38 to 39.75. Appendix C replaces approximately 8.5 plus 108 minutes with approximately 20 minutes total, without establishing comparable timing conditions. Main benchmark scores, user-study percentages, and relocated resolution-ablation values remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, rendering equations, losses, Gumbel-Softmax formulation, and inference rule in Equations 1–11 and Appendix B are retained. No new theoretical results or proofs appear.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions: orthographic pixel-art supervision, semantic preservation, and palette-constrained differentiable quantization. Claims about comparative quality, controllability, and fabrication potential remain substantively unchanged.

C2.justification: The expanded ablation discussion distinguishes component-specific failure mechanisms, including plausible individual views but inconsistent global geometry without depth loss. The limitations concerning intricate geometry, coarse resolution, and physical fabrication remain unchanged.

D1.justification: v2 specifies 1200 × 1200 rendering and clarifies palette extraction from all pixels across six views. Appendix C replaces stage-specific RTX 4090 timings with a resolution-dependent total, losing the stage breakdown. Other implementation tables and project-access information remain.

R1.justification: There are limited citation substitutions, including NeuralEditor in place of the earlier scene-operations editing reference, and Blended Diffusion in place of Blended Latent Diffusion. Most other reference changes concern bibliographic metadata; the research positioning remains stable.

P1.justification: v2 expands and reorganizes the ablation discussion, incorporates palette controllability into that section, and shortens the main user-study description while retaining appendix details. The abstract, method narrative, and overall document structure remain largely unchanged.

P2.justification: The pipeline and projection diagrams are redrawn, the component-ablation collage becomes a common-input comparison matrix, and a quantitative component table is added. The resolution table and Gumbel preference figure move to the appendix, with substantial rearrangement and some rerendering of other comparison figures.

improvement.justification: The five-object component ablations and clearer diagrams improve support for the design choices and make the method easier to assess. Headline benchmark results remain unchanged. These gains are limited by the unexplained runtime revision and loss of stage-specific timings, which prevent interpreting the new timing as a demonstrated speedup.
